frequency_question: How often does the Treasury scale up a liquidity program to a specific volume target within 131 days of initial implementation?
membership_rule: Includes all Treasury liquidity or buyback programs initiated since 2000 that involve volume-based scaling; excludes one-off emergency interventions.
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: Only two major long-term buyback programs exist in the modern era; both reached operational maturity within the 131-day window.
known_gaps: Sample size is extremely small due to the rarity of the specific program type.
skeleton: Number of liquidity program phases initiated / Number of phases reaching target volume within 131 days
validity_reason: The Treasury's operational procedures for bond management are stable over multi-year cycles.
